canonical_data: a hosted index of code, docs, datasets, and other indexed sources behind Nia's proprietary API, plus files and synced personal data that stay on the user's own machine when configured that way
current_repo_note: The nozomio-labs GitHub org hosts small open client repositories (nia-cli under Apache-2.0, plus a setup wizard, Claude Code plugin, and agent skill); the indexer, vector store, and ranking logic served from trynia.ai are closed and hosted, and self-hosted deployment of that stack is offered only as an enterprise arrangement.
strengths: Broad source coverage (code repos, documentation sites, PDFs, HuggingFace datasets, package manifests, local folders) served through one API, CLI, MCP server, and a Claude Code skill/plugin

Private repositories, files, and local folders are processed and kept on the user's machine, personal sync sources (iMessage, notes, browser history) use on-device zero-knowledge encryption, and the full indexing stack can be self-hosted

Publishes a methodology-documented hallucination/retrieval benchmark against GPT-5 and named competitors (Context7, Exa Code, Brave Search), backed by a YC-funded team shipping several open client repositories
weaknesses: The benchmark claiming the lowest error rate is self-administered by Nia against a judge model Nia also controls, with no independent reproduction found

Only thin client repositories (CLI, wizard, plugin, skill) are open; the indexer, vector store, and ranking logic that do the actual retrieval work are closed and disclosed only through the self-hosting enterprise offer
Indexed content is documented as needing periodic reindexing to stay current rather than being continuously and automatically refreshed
why_it_matters: A YC-backed retrieval layer purpose-built to sit in front of coding and research agents, notable for pairing a genuinely open CLI/MCP client with documented data-sovereignty controls and a self-hosting option alongside its proprietary hosted API.
